passages.text: The paper reports three chronically implanted participants, parallel speech and gesture decoders, restricted vocabularies, and a proof-of-concept avatar interface.
Models trained only on isolated attempts did not fully generalize to simultaneous attempts; the authors call for larger cohorts, larger repertoires and other recording methods.
NIH reports that the study used three patients, translated two participants’ activity into a full-body avatar, and used a wired system connecting implanted sensors to external processing units.

sourceSafetyLimit: A single normal-web open of the Nature primary article subsequently returned a non-retryable identity-provider redirect. No retry or alternate transport was used. The preserved normal-web search result is the permitted primary-source content used here.
claimBoundary: Report the paper as a research proof of concept for people with severe paralysis. Do not claim a consumer product, clinical availability, restored speech, or improved health outcomes.
